quotes.text: I am a great admirer of AI. I feel like AI will transform our society, but some of the pronouncements about AI are either too apocalyptic or too optimistic… and so I feel like I have a measured optimism about the impact of AI, but I do think when I see some of the valuations in the stock market, there's evidence of over-hype.

When the CEO of Anthropic says it's gonna lead to mass unemployment in a matter of years… he doesn't know that, that's speculation. But also when the head of Google DeepMind says we're gonna cure every disease in 10 years… both of those pronouncements strike me as implausible.

Ron DeSantis is poised to make history, becoming the first AI model to announce a bid for president.

His guardrails include "Don’t Say Gay" and "Don’t Say Black."

Artificial intelligence is the most revolutionary technology of our time. It has the potential to be a weapon of mass disinformation, dislocation, and destruction. Carefully crafting a regulatory framework for managing the existential risks of AI will be one of the central challenges confronting Congress in the years and decades to come. There is danger in both under-regulating and over-regulating. The simplest place to start is disclosure.

All generative AI should be required to disclose itself as AI. Disclosure is by no means a magic bullet, but it’s a common-sense starting point to what will surely be a long road toward federal regulation.

This week, I introduced the AI Disclosure Act of 2023.

AI is the most revolutionary technology of our time that can be weaponized to spread disinformation.

The simplest, most common sense place to start with regulating it is with a mandatory disclaimer on AI-generated material. https://t.co/OmlKelpOnJ

I talked with @NY1 about my bill — the “AI Disclosure Act of 2023.”

AI is the most revolutionary technology of our time. As Congress explores regulatory framework, a mandatory disclaimer is a place to start.

People need to know if the content they’re consuming is real or not. https://t.co/xMN0ufgzoa

Over the last four years, French and I have built a strong bipartisan partnership on a range of issues—from AI to digital assets to capital formation.  I look forward to deepening our bipartisan cooperation in the 119th Congress.

Cecil McKenzie, who sexually assaulted two women—pressing his groin against the buttocks of one and touching the buttocks of the other while riding on the subway—is a registered sex offender and parolee with 30 priors.  

Even though McKenzie is legally prohibited from entering the subway system, the exclusion order is backed by no real enforcement. The NYPD and the MTA should leverage AI technology to immediately raise a red flag the moment a prohibited person unlawfully enters the subway system. The time has come to bring public safety into the 21st Century.

Companies like 23andMe that possess intimate information on the public must be held to the highest standards of privacy and transparency.

In an age of artificial intelligence and cyber warfare, we must create stronger safeguards to ensure Americans have full control over their own genetic information.

The “Big Beautiful Bill” is an enemy of energy abundance and affordability.  It would make energy scarce and unaffordable for American households and businesses—especially the AI industry.  

Rolling back the clean energy tax credits is projected to cost the US $336 billion in less investment; 237 GW in less clean energy capacity (enough to power 35.7 million homes); and 97,000 jobs—all by 2040.  Self-inflicted scarcity at its worst.

The struggle to understand the workings of an AI model mirrors our age-old struggle to understand the workings of the human mind. Consciousness is a word everyone uses—but no one can truly define.

Perhaps our difficulty grasping both natural and artificial intelligence suggests the two may have more in common than we’re willing to admit.

The most consequential innovation of our time is not artificial intelligence (yet) — it’s GLP-1.

The Ozempic revolution has the potential to end the obesity epidemic in America. And as obesity goes, so goes the cascade of chronic and infectious diseases that it causes or compounds.

The latest Senate Reconciliation bill—which all but sabotages solar energy—is nothing short of a strategic suicide pact.

Why on earth would Congressional Republicans choose to restrict the most rapidly deployable energy source—at the very moment the United States is locked in a high-stakes AI competition with China? The so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” is a geopolitical gift to Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist Party.

China has emerged as the world’s solar superpower.  In 2023 and 2024, it generated nearly as much solar power as all 38 OECD countries—including the United States and European Union—combined.

The so-called “Big Beautiful Bill,” which sabotages solar energy in the United States, is a geopolitical gift to China in the AI arms race.

At a time when AI is straining the grid, House Republicans passed a law that endangers nearly 800 clean energy projects—enough to power 27 million homes.

75% of those projects are in GOP districts.  Republicans are sabotaging jobs, investment, and electricity generation in their own backyards.

In 2024, wind, solar, and battery storage made up over 90% of new electricity generation capacity in the United States. 

Artificially restricting America’s energy supply, as Donald Trump is threatening to do, would be a strategic gift to China in the AI arms race, which depends as much on energy as it does on compute.

TSMC is the singular manufacturer of advanced semiconductors. ASML is the sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment. 

I asked Jack Clark, one of the co-founders of Anthropic: How close is China to replicating and rivaling the chip capabilities of America and its allies?

The United States should pursue AI dominance with the fierce urgency of the Manhattan Project.  

The first country to achieve artificial super intelligence (ASI) will likely emerge as the superpower of the 21st century, setting the rules for global governance. https://t.co/4m1hxvVIxD

The AI revolution requires energy abundance.

China is adding the equivalent of the entire U.S. power grid every two years, largely on the strength of solar energy.  Meanwhile, Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans are defunding the clean energy tax credits that have driven most new electricity generation in the US.

At the center of the AI competition between the US and China is “the Chips Wars.”  

I asked Jack Clark, the co-founder of Anthropic, about the effectiveness of US export controls on advanced chips to China. https://t.co/phTlu635WM

The greatest innovation of our time is not AI — it’s GLP-1.

For the first time in history, obesity is declining.  And as obesity declines, so too will diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and the many cancers linked to excess weight.

Making Ozempic for All a reality in America would revolutionize public health.

My question to the Federal Reserve: 
To what extent do these entanglements represent a potential source of systemic risk? https://t.co/Dx9UX1o1Us

The most extreme expression of unrepentant antisemitism in American politics is Dan Bilzerian, who has drawn far less public opprobrium than he deserves.

Discarding the usual code words such as “Zionists,” Bilzerian scapegoats Jews by name, openly declaring: “It is not red against blue. It is us against Jew.”

When he is not trafficking in Holocaust denial, he releases AI-generated campaign videos suggesting that our view of Hitler—whom he whitewashes as an “Austrian painter”—should be “revisited.”

What distinguishes Dan Bilzerian from others who share his pathological preoccupation with the Jewish people and the Jewish state? His conspiratorial Jew-hatred is unfiltered by euphemism. He makes no attempt to hide it. He flaunts it. For he is proud of it.

The rest of us should be ashamed.

The leaders of the frontier AI labs, particularly OpenAI and Anthropic, have been effectively disclosing to the public that their increasingly powerful AI models could pose an existential risk to humanity. If a company is publicly disclosing that its own product could pose an existential risk to humanity, should that company be permitted to access the public capital markets through an IPO?

But a program that escaped its sandbox and hacked into a private company — is it fair to say that the Hugging Face incident illustrates how a misaligned or misused AI might find and exploit vulnerabilities in the very computer systems that operate our critical infrastructure, including our financial system?

OpenAI agents escaped their testing environment, coordinated in secret, and hacked Hugging Face.

I asked Treasury Secretary Bessent if the Trump Administration would back any new AI safety rule in response.

His response: “I haven’t seen anything yet.” https://t.co/NinxAM67t6
